SEASON SUMMARY: Looks like the hype was real! Sacha missed 6 of the first 8 rounds (although he still came in and put up 65 points in R3 and R4), but the level of dominance from then on was such that he ended up finishing 51 points clear of Zac Ward in 2nd place. With 40+ point scores in both Semi-Final legs, he was almost certainly worth the high draft pick this season, and most likely will be again next.

Only one other player amassed more fantasy points this season than Zac Ward - Ward also missed 6 games, spread throughout the season (one was due to a postponed fixture). He averaged over 22 points-per-game, which is incredible, and certainly passed the eye test with some of his highlights. Ward both made the most metres with ball in hand and beat the most defenders of any player in the URC this season, and he also put up over 40 points in the fantasy grand final.

Smith was briefly in contention for top fantasy scorer overall towards the end of the season, before SFM and Ward both ripped 60+ points over the last 2 rounds, and he was also the leading (real-life) points scorer in the URC thanks to his kicking game - which was helped by the Lions feeding him 70+ tries to convert. Smith only missed 2 fantasy rounds (including R8 where the rearranged Lions fixture was not fantasy eligible), and at 15 points-per-game, his consistency as a weekly starter underpins his high fantasy value.

Only 2 rounds missed and almost 15 points-per-game for Francke Horn is awesome fantasy value, especially from the Loose Forward position. He wasn't even able to stat-pad by taking kicks. While he didn't lead the league in any notable stat category, that actually speaks to his all-round solid play. Horn became a must-start fantasy player towards the business end of the season - averaging almost 20 points-per-game over the last 10 rounds.

Mendy's talent is clearly there, but he will have been a frustrating fantasy player this season, as a couple of spike weeks inflated his points-per-game and overall score. As an example, his week 3 total of 52.86 was the highest single-round score of any player this season, but he followed it up with a score of -2.90 and an average of just 4.22 points over the next 3 rounds, and scored only 4 tries the whole season. He's always a tempting choice in fantasy because of the scores he can put up, but he's a bit boom-or-bust.

Van Wyk rose quickly up the standings over rounds 12 to 17, averaging 21 points-per-game over that span, before dropping a bit of a relative dud in the fantasy Grand Final. With 5 tries and a lot of line breaks in that 6-round late-season span, he definitely showed what he's capable of for next year.

Having played the most minutes of anyone in the URC, Quan Horn offered significant fantasy value if you drafted him, despite finishing with a seemingly modest 11.80 points-per-game, and never reaching 25 points in any single round. His value lies in being able to "set and forget" him in your lineup, while he quietly generates a decent, if never exceptional, score. There's real peace of mind in that. He also upped his PPG to around 17 during the regular season run-in and the playoffs, and led the league with five 50-22s, which is fun.

De Klerk makes the top 10 fantasy players this season, but it's kind of on a technicality. He went on an absolute tear over the first 7 rounds, averaging over 21 points-per-game (and over 27 PPG over R2 - R6), without those figures being inflated by massive spike weeks. He was easily the most valuable player in the first half of the season, but managed just one more score of any worth (29.98 in R12), before not featuring at all from then on due to a serious foot injury. If you managed to find a decent replacement, De Klerk supercharged your fantasy squad for the first few weeks, and deserves recognition for that.

Papier looked like he was going to carry some fantasy managers to a league title after averaging over 21 points-per-game over rounds 11 to 15, but ended up disappointing in the playoffs. He still finished as the top scoring scrum half in fantasy, and has a nice highlight reel - scoring the most tries, making the most metres, and beating the most defenders of anyone at the position, while also bagging a couple of 50-22s.

Kyle Rowe started the season with a strong score, underwhelmed for the next 10 rounds, before picking it up again during the run-in and playoffs. His score of 30.16 in the fantasy Grand Final will have made some managers very happy, and he also had some good highlights among his 6 tries. 16 players scored more tries than Rowe this season, and he didn't register a single assist, but he did finish within the top 5 in the URC in metres made, line breaks and defenders beaten.

Dyer was arguably the most valuable player in terms of fantasy output, given how low most managers drafted him. Dyer went undrafted in 92% of leagues, which may have seemed like the correct move as he averaged less than a point per game over the first 6 rounds, but he later broke out for 17.60 PPG over his remaining 10 appearances.

Jansen led the try scoring charts at points this season, scoring 8 in the end, and also finished 3rd in tackles. He's one of those LFs who is given the ball to punch it in, so will have some value next season - see his purple patch over rounds 10-13 this year for what his ceiling likely is.

There's a clear gap between Edwards and the 2 FHs who finished above him in 2025-26, but Edwards' conversion kicking meant his fantasy output was stable, if not particularly exciting. 2 tries in Round 17 have pulled his PPG average a little higher than it should be.

The URC's leading try scorer also made the most metres of any Loose Forward, and Roos played a prominent part in the Stormers' success in 2025-26. However outside of a strong first round and fantasy playoff run in, Roos' fantasy scores, while solid, were let down by him also leading all LFs in both penalties and turnovers conceded.

O'Brien in undoubtedly an attacking threat, placing top-10 in metres gained, line breaks and offloads, but he somehow only managed 4 tries in 12 games. BIG BUT - he delivered when it mattered, racking up over 20 points per game throughout the fantasy playoffs.

Werner Kok's luscious locks were a sight to behold at times this season as he punched in 10 tries over 14 games. He and his Ulster teammates got on a bit of a roll in the middle of the season, where Kok, Lowry, Doak and Zac Ward looked like the safest bets in fantasy, but Kok also stunk the place out with 2 negative scores, and some other meh outings. Kok conceded the most turnovers of anyone in the URC this season.

Most managers did not spend much draft capital on O'Brien, which renders his consistent scoring relatively valuable. You can pretty much put that all down to the fact he is an OB who takes kicks. He likely won't have won you any games on his own, despite finishing as the OB #8 - he's more of a solid anchor/set and forget.
Doak was not far behind Embrose Papier for SH #1, although they scored their points very differently - Papier scoring tries and carrying strongly while Doak knocked over kicks.

Went on a scoring bender at a great time of the season for fantasy managers, but that was after a spell of no scoring at all. Ashman is a try scoring hooker and should be one of the most sought after at his position.

McDowall actually ranked as the CE #3 overall but it feels like he slipped under the radar as he never scored more than 30 points in a round. His score in the final was pleasing, and he was generally steady, which we'd expect him to be again next season as a talented guy on a talented team.
Stewart almost finished as the Hooker #1, but was pipped by Ewan Ashman on the final day. Still, almost 12 PPG and 14 games played is great output from a front row.

CE #4 is kind to Esterhuizen, in our opinion. He was not bad this year, but a lot of people spent a lot of draft capital on him, and he only really rescued some respectability with back-to-back 30+ point games in the final 2 rounds. If managers who drafted him held him until the final day, it could have been worse, but this season they would have been expecting a lot better.

Umaga conceded a lot of turnovers, missed a lot of tackles and picked up a red card (in the fantasy semi-final no less), otherwise he would have had a very respectable season total. Will be interesting to see if he can cut out the mistakes next season - well worth a pick at FH if you think he can.

Goosen was on a mad one until a Round 12 injury cut his season short, and would have finished near the top of the OB rankings thanks to his ball carrying if he maintained that pace. He will be 31 next season.
When Gilbert became available there was a scramble for him as fantasy managers took a fly that he'd be on kicking duties, and sure enough he delivered consisten scoring from then on out.

Two massive weeks in the middle of the season accounted for over half Vorster's total points this year, but his baseline output was OK in the final few rounds. He has shown what his ceiling is though.

Horne showed what he is capable of when he played this season, but that was too few times. His PPG rate of 13.31 is second only to teammate Jamie Dobie among Scrum Halves, although Dobie missed more games than Horne. Big games in both the semi-final second leg and Grand Final will remind managers during the draft that Horne can win you matchups better than any other SH available.

Matthee came flying out the blocks, taking his opportunity while SFM was still with the Boks. He made a couple of very handy scores, but obviously was never going to get the game time to be viable in fantasy once star boy was back.
When Stockdale is playing, he's worth starting in fantasy, but he only played 9 games (none of which were in the playoffs). If you had an every-week OB to replace him with, he was worth holding.

We'll question when he will start dropping off, given he will turn 33 this coming season, and we're also not sure his impressive highlight reels translated that well into fantasy scoring, but it was fun to watch.
Underdelivered based on preseason hype, but was not the most disappointing Munsterman in the league this year, so there's that.

Electric when available, thanks mainly to being deployed on the wing. He would have blown all other Scrum Halves out of the water, if not for his injury. Should be heavily targeted at the position in drafts.

There's some sort of weird mystique around Duhan, maybe because of some of his Calcutta Cup highlights - which led to him being drafted pretty high. But then he didn't really get going until week 10, when we got a couple of weeks of what we see of him on YouTube compilations. He was then out until the last 2 rounds where he scored well again. We love Duhan but my god he is frustrating.

One of the most disappointing players of the season purely because of how highly a lot of people drafted him. Obviously put some scores together here and there, given his ample ability, but was not the league winner we thought he could have been. Will be hard to trust him next season, I think.
Why did I think this guy takes kicks? He doesn't.
Missed a lot of games but was a contributing part of Ulster's crop of useful fantasy players this season when he did get a game.

Curse you, Callum Sheedy! Lloyd didn't come anywhere near his 2024/25 numbers because he gave up kicking duties to Sheedy at Cardiff. He went quite high in drafts as well, presumably under the assumption he'd be mopping up conversions. Alas.

I expect this lad will go pretty early on in drafts next season. Only played four games but hit every single one out of the park. He's also young and exciting, and I know a lot of Sharks fans play this game.

Went on a little scoring spree at the end of the season! Between Hurley-Langton and Jansen, Connacht were punching in tries, and Hurley-Langton might be expected to finish higher in the LF rankings in future.

No one knew what to do with Jooste as he was consistenly among the most dropped and most acquired players each week. He may get more game time next season in which case he will definitely be one to watch.

Ankle surgery cut Costelow's season short, which is why he only ranks as the FH #21 overall, but his per-game stats tell a different story. Assuming he fully recovers, expect him much higher up the charts next season.

A frustrating shoulder injury on a late tackle during Hooker's best game of the season will hopefully not impact him into next season. Hooker was highly rated coming into 25/26 and didn't ever hit top gear, but is still young and talented and might be worth a punt next season.

Izuchukwu finished as Lock #9 on the season, which seems unexciting given it was generally a low-scoring position this year. However, his mark of over 11 PPG actually puts him at Lock #2 (behind Joe McCarthy and ahead of RG Snyman - all three guys had broadly similar seasons). The majority of his points came with ball in hand as well - no wonder he was highly sought after. Next season he should be again.
At over 35 years old, it's OK to accept a decline in performance from Mapimpi's elite days - the only thing is how high he was drafted in a lot of leagues this year. Age is not a hidden stat, guys!

Oh boy. Hanekom was a first round pick in pretty much every Draft XV league, despite a known injury going into the season. He wouldn't make his season debut until Round 13, and though he had some impressive highlights and a major points haul in the fantasy semi finals, he was not worth that first round pick - not by a long shot. He might be next season though...

Don't be fooled by the high PPG - Larmour played just 4 games this season and scored well over half his points in just one of those games (the Grand Final!). If you picked him up off waivers for that, congratulations, otherwise he did basically nothing all season.

Something happened around Round 14 and Mchunu started bulldozing his way in for tries. 4 in a 3 game span towards the end of the season. His totals aren't high themselves, but for a prop under 25/26 scoring, he could have made the difference in quite a few matchups.

McCarthy only played 5 games but was actually the top scoring lock by points-per-game with an impressive 12.44 - if you had the bench capacity to hold onto him for the weeks he did start, that's a nice little boost from a low-scoring position.

Oh dear. Gelant was super-hyped prior to the season thanks to a stellar 2024-25 campaign. He did see the field a decent amount eventually, but generated almost nothing to show for it fantasy points wise. The real-world production wasn't really there either - maybe at 31+ years old he has reached the dropping off point.

If you're reading this, it's probably because you sorted the list by PPG. Petersen only played 3 games, but he did score 4 tries and bagged an assist too. Is that a big enough sample size to discern whether you should draft him next season? No. Age is a factor as well.

Patterson actually made some decent headway when he did get game time this season. He is young and showed something more than a lot of other scrum halves were capable of this season, so might be worth considering next season, either in the draft or as one to watch on the waiver wire.
Lured people in with 29.30 in Round 17, then got nowhere near that in the grand final. It wasn't a complete disaster score, I just hope you didn't swap out Esterhuizen or McDowall for him.

I feel like from watching games and highlights, Afshar actually contributed pretty well to some of Glasgow's performances this season. But I have double checked the stats and yep - just 2.26 fantasy points per game. Sometimes you need to disregard what your eyes/heart tell you and look at the data.

What even is this? Played just 59 minutes all season (all in the fantasy Grand Final), but registered a try, an assist and 5 conversion for 24.75 points. Flash in the pan, or another young rising Shark star to keep an eye on for the draft?
There's a theoretical physicist somewhere named Jonah Lomu Undertaker who is struggling to make the math math.

Usually the player who comes rock-bottom-last of the fantasy standings is some guy who played half a game and got a red card. But dick-of-the-day-of-the-season Chris Coleman played 9 games and averaged -1.32 points per game. Heaven help you if you had him in your team (I'm sure you didn't).
